headline: NgramRL uses prior rollouts to accelerate structured RL post-training generation
summary: NgramRL proposes per-prompt CPU-side n-gram caches built from recent policy rollouts, with target-model verification and an adaptive fan-out prefetcher that prepares likely next drafts during GPU work. In author-reported experiments across Qwen3-8B and DeepSeek-LLM-7B on GSM8K, Spider and CodeContests, it commits 3.60–7.77 tokens per target forward in the final 30% of training, depending on model/task, versus 2.32–4.15 for SuffixDecoding. On Spider, prefetch improves rollout throughput over synchronous NgramRL by 1.38x for Qwen3-8B and 1.21x for DeepSeek-7B at budget N=16. These are paper-reported results, not independent replication or end-to-end training-cost measurements.
